Assume Countable Choice. Fix $m\ge1$ and angles $0<\theta_j<\pi$ for $1\le j\le m$. On the strip $S=\mathbb R\times[0,1]$ impose the real product-plane boundary conditions $u(s,0)\in\mathbb R^m$ and $u(s,1)\in\prod_j e^{i\theta_j}\mathbb R$. Let $H^1_\theta$ be the completion of smooth maps satisfying these conditions and compactly supported in the $s$ direction, for the norm
$$\|u\|_{H^1}^2=\|u\|_2^2+\|u_s\|_2^2+\|u_t\|_2^2.$$
The real linear operator $D=\partial_s+i\partial_t$ extends to an isomorphism $H^1_\theta\to L^2(S;\mathbb C^m)$. Put $\gamma=\min_j\{\theta_j,\pi-\theta_j\}>0$. Its inverse satisfies
$$\|D^{-1}f\|_2\le\gamma^{-1}\|f\|_2,\qquad \|D^{-1}f\|_{H^1}\le\sqrt{\gamma^{-2}+5}\,\|f\|_2.$$
For $0\le\delta<\gamma$, set $w(s)=e^{\delta|s|}$, $H^1_{\theta,\delta}=\{u:wu\in H^1_\theta\}$ with norm $\|wu\|_{H^1}$, and $L^2_\delta=\{f:wf\in L^2\}$ with norm $\|wf\|_2$. Then $D:H^1_{\theta,\delta}\to L^2_\delta$ is an isomorphism and
$$\|D^{-1}f\|_{H^1_{\theta,\delta}}\le\frac{\sqrt{\gamma^{-2}+5}}{1-\delta/\gamma}\,\|f\|_{L^2_\delta},\qquad \|wD^{-1}f\|_2\le\frac{\|wf\|_2}{\gamma-\delta}.$$
These are estimates for the constant linear asymptotic model. They make no assertion about nonlinear strip decay, a variable-coefficient operator, or its Maslov index.

derivations.claim: Parametrize the second circle by $(r,3\varepsilon r)$ modulo $\mathbb Z^2$. It meets the first exactly when $3r$ is an integer. Modulo its period one these give $r=0,1/3,2/3$, and the tangent vectors $(1,0),(1,3\varepsilon)$ are independent. The inverse images in the plane of the two circles are respectively the disjoint lines $y=a$, $a\in\mathbb Z$, and $3\varepsilon x-y=b$, $b\in\mathbb Z$. For the latter assertion, its primitive integer normal vector is $(3\varepsilon,-1)$; its integer level lines are exactly the lattice translates of its real direction line. Thus each fixed pair of lifts intersects once, at $y=a$, $x=(a+b)/(3\varepsilon)$. [given, construct, algebra]

Every continuous disk map $v$ to this torus has a continuous plane lift; here is an explicit construction without a general covering-classification theorem. Regard the source as a convex round disk and fix a source point $p_0$ and one lift $V_0$ of $v(p_0)$. In the flat quotient metric, two points at distance less than $1/4$ have a unique difference vector with both coordinates in $(-1/2,1/2)$; call it $d(a,b)$, pointing from $a$ to $b$. This vector depends continuously on such pairs, as is checked in ordinary small coordinate squares of the quotient. Uniform continuity on the compact source gives an integer $N$ such that adjacent points of every equally subdivided segment from $p_0$ to any $p$ have images this close. Explicitly choose the subdivision mesh smaller than a uniform-continuity radius; a uniform radius follows from a finite subcover by the inverse images of small torus coordinate squares. Put $p_j=(1-j/N)p_0+(j/N)p$ and $$V(p)=V_0+\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}d(v(p_j),v(p_{j+1})).$$ It is continuous and its quotient is $v(p)$ by telescoping. A lift of a smooth map is smooth locally because the quotient is a local translation diffeomorphism. Any two lifts of the same map differ by a continuous integer vector and hence by a constant on a connected source. All selections here were finite. [given, construct, algebra]

We verify the periodic-domain assertion directly. In the plane, the complementary regions are the parallelograms $a<y<a+1$, $b<3\varepsilon x-y<b+1$, for integers $a,b$. Each projects injectively to the torus: a difference by $(l,k)\in\mathbb Z^2$ within one such region forces $k=0$ from the first inequalities, then $l=0$ from the second. There are three quotient regions, since shifting $a$ to zero leaves $b$ modulo three. The integral of each of the closed one-forms $dx,dy$ around every region boundary is zero, by the ordinary coordinate fundamental theorem on its plane parallelogram. Hence if a periodic domain has boundary $c\alpha+d\beta_\varepsilon$, these integrals give $c+d=0$ and $3\varepsilon d=0$. Thus $c=d=0$. Its region coefficients are consequently equal on opposite sides of every edge. They are all equal because a path between any two region interiors on the connected torus can be chosen to cross the finite edges away from vertices; equivalently the three explicit parallelograms have connected adjacency graph. The zero basepoint coefficient therefore makes the entire domain zero. This calculation assumes no domain-index formula or admissibility theorem. [step 1.1, construct, algebra]

Lift a relative disk by step 1.2. On its first boundary arc the second coordinate of the lift is a continuous integer-valued function, so it is one constant $a$. On its second arc $3\varepsilon V_x-V_y$ is likewise one integer $b$. Therefore both lifted endpoints lie at the unique intersection of these two affine lines from step 1.1. Their projections must coincide, proving impossibility when $x\ne y$. In the remaining case call that intersection $c$. The affine homotopy $V_h=(1-h)V+hc$ fixes both endpoints and keeps each boundary arc in its own affine line. Its quotient is an actual relative homotopy to the constant disk at $x$. Thus the relative class assertion has been proved directly; no assertion about periodic domains or Maslov grading formulas was used. [step 1.1, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

A strip with uniform ends compactifies continuously to such a disk: the explicit maps $z=e^{\pi(s+it)}$ and $z\mapsto(z-i)/(z+i)$ identify its interior with a round disk and its two ends with distinct boundary points. Its lift can equivalently be restricted from the compact-disk lift in step 1.2, so the lifted strip $V$ has both ends equal to $c$ and its boundaries on the two corresponding lines. Subtract $c$ and call the map $W$. The quotient is locally holomorphic with derivative the identity, hence $W_s+iW_t=0$. Its flat energy is unchanged by lifting, and $W$ tends uniformly to zero at both ends. For the real one-form $\lambda=(x\,dy-y\,dx)/2$ on the plane, direct differentiation gives $$\partial_s\lambda(W_t)-\partial_t\lambda(W_s)=\det(W_s,W_t)=|W_s|^2,$$ since the equation gives $W_t=iW_s$. On either horizontal edge $W$ and its tangential derivative lie in a single real line through zero, so $\lambda(W_s)=0$. Integrating the displayed identity on any finite strip rectangle by two one-variable fundamental theorems therefore expresses its nonnegative energy $\int|W_s|^2$ as the difference of the two vertical-edge integrals of $\lambda$. This proves the needed area identity without a stronger-choice Stokes supplier. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

Finite energy makes $f(s)=\int_0^1|W_t(s,t)|^2dt$ integrable and continuous. Choose $S_n\in(n,n+1)$ and $R_n\in(n,n+1)$ so $f(S_n),f(-R_n)$ tend to zero. Such choices can be specified as the first rationals whose values are smaller than twice the corresponding interval integral plus $1/n$, because the average argument and continuity give a nonempty open set of such values. The vertical boundary integrals in step 3.1 have absolute values at most $$\tfrac12\sup_{0\le t\le1}|W(s,t)|\, f(s)^{1/2}.$$ They tend to zero at $s=S_n,-R_n$ by the uniform ends. The increasing rectangles $[-R_n,S_n]\times[0,1]$ exhaust the strip. Their nonnegative energy integrals therefore have limit zero, so the smooth nonnegative density $|W_s|^2$ vanishes identically. The equation gives $W_t=0$ as well. Thus every such actual strip is constant. This proof does not assume that all representatives in a null relative class are constant; it proves the assertion for the actual flat holomorphic equation. [step 3.1, given, construct, algebra]

At a constant strip the geometric operator is exactly $D_0=\partial_s+i\partial_t$, with lower boundary line $\mathbb R$ and upper line of direction $1+3\varepsilon i$. The latter equals $e^{i\theta}\mathbb R$, with $\theta=\arctan3$ if $\varepsilon=1$ and $\theta=\pi-\arctan3$ if $\varepsilon=-1$. Both angles lie strictly between zero and $\pi$. The actual inverse [F1] consequently proves surjectivity and zero kernel, hence real index zero. Together with step 4.1 this leaves no actual index-one solution. The empty count is finite and zero for every basepoint restriction, and the three-element generator module from step 1.1 has zero differential and therefore three-dimensional homology. The sign choice was retained throughout, so the calculation treats both diagrams. Only Countable Choice, the explicitly stated linear supplier and finite or rational-recursive constructions were used. No closed-manifold invariance theorem was inferred. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 4.1, construct, algebra] ∎

boundaries.reason: The Statement concerns the fixed nonempty torus and exactly three transverse generators.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement and periodic-domain proof identify the zero-basepoint periodic domain with zero; the actual differential is the empty zero count.
The Statement covers one generator endpoint repeated at both ends; the relative lift contraction and actual area argument explicitly treat that case.

boundaries.reason: The Statement has fixed transverse primitive lines with determinant plus or minus three; tangent or parallel circles are not asserted inputs.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement and energy proof retain uniform ends; the compact disk lift fixes both ends at the unique affine-line intersection.
The Statement and proof use finitely subdivided radial paths and first rational slice choices, avoiding an arbitrary covering classification theorem under AC.
